note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Adaptive partitioning for optimistic optimization: motivation, algorithms, theory and benchmark results

nodes.name: Optimistic optimization needs a partition
nodes.description: Optimistic Optimization algorithms (HOO, SOO, SequOOL) assume only local smoothness around the maximizer but require a hierarchical partitioning of the search space, and their performance depends heavily on that partitioning.

nodes.name: Default axis-aligned partition is limiting
nodes.description: The default axis-aligned rectangle partitioning has a number of cells growing as k^(dn), limiting it to low-dimensional spaces, and may fail to exploit low-dimensional structure in high-dimensional spaces.

nodes.name: Multi-index function class
nodes.description: The paper studies multi-index functions f(x)=g(Ax) with A an m x d matrix with orthonormal rows and m<d, whose variation lies in an m-dimensional subspace.

nodes.name: Optimizer lies in a bounded subspace region
nodes.description: For a multi-index function on [-1,1]^d, some z* in R^m with ||z*||_inf at most alpha satisfies f(A^T z*)=f(x*), where alpha is chosen from the cube corners (Proposition 2.5).

nodes.name: Adaptive partitioning scheme
nodes.description: An adaptive partitioning scheme partitions the m-dimensional projection of the domain using learned directions A-hat, and a direction selection strategy can choose which direction to split at each depth.

nodes.name: Learning A by a one-hidden-layer network
nodes.description: Algorithm 1 learns A-hat by fitting a single hidden-layer neural network to function evaluations at random locations and taking an SVD, with m chosen to explain a desired share (e.g. 95%) of variation.

nodes.name: Adaptive scheme can lower rho
nodes.description: Adaptive partitions can have better parameters than the default: for f=1-|x1+x2| with A=[1,1], rho_A=1/3 versus rho=1/sqrt(3) for the default scheme (Example 2.9).

nodes.name: Direction selection can lower eta
nodes.description: A direction selection strategy that splits x1 twice as often as x2 yields a lower near-optimality dimension than the default equal-proportion splitting (Example 2.11).

nodes.name: Two algorithms
nodes.description: The paper proposes a two-stage algorithm (learn the partition, then run SequOOL on it) and an interleaved algorithm (Algorithm 2) where learning and optimization alternate.

nodes.name: Lower regret for multi-index functions
nodes.description: For multi-index functions, SequOOL on the learned partition with alpha-hat=sqrt(dm)/sqrt(1-dist^2(A,A-hat)) has lower regret than on the default partition, with regret ~O(n^(-beta/d)) (Theorem 4.8).

nodes.name: Synthetic benchmark gains
nodes.description: On Rastrigin, Sphere and Styblinski-Tang, the approach reaches zero regret with fewer samples than other methods, e.g. Rastrigin regret 4.22e-5 for SequOOL vs zero for the method, and zero regret on Styblinski-Tang with about 900 evaluations versus 2000 for RESOO.

nodes.name: Joint LLM quantization objective
nodes.description: Quantization scales alpha across all M layers of an LLM are jointly optimized to minimize perplexity as one 3M-dimensional black-box problem, instead of AWQ's 3M separate 1-D grid searches.

nodes.name: Improved OPT-1.3B perplexity
nodes.description: On OPT-1.3B, SequOOL with Algorithm 2 over 72 dimensions reaches WikiText-2 perplexity 16.68 versus 16.92 for AWQ grid search, narrowing the gap to the unquantized 14.47 from 2.45 to 2.21 (about 10% relative).

isolated_nodes.name: Weaker on some functions
isolated_nodes.description: On Ellipsoid, Sharp Ridge and (x1-1)^2+(x72-1)^4, the algorithm is slightly worse than RESOO, plausibly because 650 samples of a 2000 budget go to the first stage.

isolated_nodes.name: Limited benefit without multi-index structure
isolated_nodes.description: When the multi-index assumption fails, as in the AWQ objective that varies in all directions, improvement over SequOOL is minimal.

isolated_nodes.name: Compute time
isolated_nodes.description: Wall-clock times are about 9 hours for grid search, 10 for SequOOL and Algorithm 1, and 12 for Algorithm 2.

structural_reasoning: Motivation about default partitions leads to adaptive partition definitions, algorithms and the regret theorem, then empirical results. The limitation and cost notes are isolated.
